correctness.rationale: The exact domain k>=2, n>=k(k+1) is fixed. The proof excludes 0<=t<=k and t>=k+2 defender blocks using explicit counts of forbidden zero assignments. In the remaining case the total-Roman condition forces k+1 disjoint k-sets. Count and degree follow from unique block partitions. At s=k the partition into k+2 equal blocks is a complete component invariant. For s>=k+1, occupied/free element transpositions connect TJ states; KG(n-k²,k) connectivity on at least 2k+1 points converts each TJ move to slides. The standalone verifier rebuilt the original predicate and exact component graph on k=2,n=6..10; check code actually ran to VERIFY_OK. Finite tests are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The precise mobility of *minimum* Roman defenses is a natural robustness and configuration-space question. The all-k component phase transition, exact edge degree, and complete split into equal-block partition cliques at a sharp integer boundary are structural facts not obtained from the scalar domination optimum. It is not a routine one-parameter bound or an arbitrary sample case; it distinguishes immobilized, partition-locked, and fully mobile regimes in an infinite two-parameter family.
